name: Political position from election results

measures.definition: An estimate of where the place voted at its latest national lower-house election, 0 left to 10 right: each party's ParlGov 2024 position (the mean of expert surveys, or of its party family where no survey covers it; an alliance takes its members' mean) averaged by its share of the official result.

coverage.geography: 18 countries with an official result read and enough of the vote positioned; Swiss cantons, Canadian provinces and Australian states. No figure for Hungary, Italy and Japan (under 75% of the vote positioned), the United States and Singapore (no ParlGov positions), Spain and Greece (official results not readable for this release) or the UAE.

rights.attribution: Borgo contributors, from official election results and ParlGov party positions (Döring, Huber and Manow, ParlGov 2024 release, CC0)

vetted.notes: Inputs, each open: ParlGov 2024 release (Döring and Manow, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/2VZ5ZC, CC0), matched by ParlGov party id; official results from each country's electoral authority or statistics office, listed with their URLs in pipeline/inputs/politics.json and docs/positions.md, each compared with its source on the date given. Wikidata and the MIT Election Lab are no longer used. The Manifesto Project was left out: its terms forbid redistribution.

caveats: Party positions are ParlGov's 2024 release: expert surveys up to about 2019, so a party that moved since keeps its older place. Where no survey covers a party, ParlGov gives its party family's mean; the note marks those parties.
A party ParlGov does not place has no position, and a place gets no figure when parties with a position took under 75% of the vote. Independents and non-party candidates have no position.

Sweden's shares are the Election Authority's rounded percentages and Switzerland's the Federal Statistical Office's party strength; France's groups are the Interior Ministry's candidate classifications (nuances).
